VOID · In active development

scores.voidVOID
# Count scores that meet the minimum.
func entry(minimum: i32) -> i32:
    var scores = [12, 18, 25]
    var qualified = 0
    for score in scores:
        if score >= minimum:
            qualified += 1
    return qualified

A LANGUAGE FOR YOUR NEXT IDEA

Clear source.
Real capabilities.

Build games, applications, tools and systems with a language designed to keep everyday code approachable and its behavior explicit.

01

Native execution

Compile to native code through one shared LLVM JIT/AOT pipeline. Run compiled source during development or emit objects for a linked executable.

Explore native compilation ↗
02

Types that express intent

Value structs, managed objects, concrete generics and structural interfaces give data and behavior clear, predictable boundaries.

Understand values and objects ↗
03

Readable, useful syntax

Work with collections and ordered dictionaries. Use enum payloads, results and pattern matching to make alternatives explicit.

Explore pattern matching ↗
04

Memory with clear ownership

Tracing garbage collection manages object memory. Scope-owned with/deinit cleanup releases resources deterministically; GC does not replace that lifetime.

Learn resource cleanup ↗
05

Async work, kept together

Use async/await for cooperative tasks and task groups for related work. Scope exit joins children; cooperative scheduling is distinct from CPU parallelism.

Follow structured tasks ↗
06

Independent native workers

Use spawn for supported CPU work on bounded native workers. The current subset transfers safe values and restricts shared mutable references.

See the worker boundary ↗

Complete source, a single integer input and a verified result. These programs use the current synchronous entry adapter; public builds are not available yet.

One choice, a concrete type.

Generic type inference keeps the chosen stock count an integer. An unavailable count falls back to zero, without an implicit type conversion.

Understand generic functions ↗

Give each state a name.

A shipment is waiting or ready with an item count. Pattern matching handles both states and names the payload only where it exists.

FEEDBACK THAT UNDERSTANDS YOUR CODE

One language service.
Closer to your ideas.

Editor feedback comes from the compiler’s understanding of VOID source, so navigation and code intelligence follow the language’s own rules.

Understand. Navigate. Refine.

Completion, hover information, signature help, definitions and references, and document and workspace symbols are implemented in the compiler-owned language server. Project queries follow the selected entry’s reachable source graph.

Guarded rename covers supported functions and bindings. Conservative four-space formatting preserves tokens, comments and imports; it does not promise a full reflow or general code actions.

Explore editor tooling ↗

Meet your editor where it is.

VS Code and Neovim adapters include guards for version-sensitive edits. Vim uses yegappan/lsp for the shared language service, with rename disabled because its edit-safety contract differs.

These integrations have local Linux execution evidence. VSCodium is an integration target with execution still unverified. New Windows/macOS editor combinations and clean-machine distribution also remain unverified.

See current development ↗
Implemented locally; broader validation is pending.

Tooling is in development and awaits hosted cross-platform acceptance. No public compiler or editor builds are distributed here.
